translations.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,
to the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be saints, together with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, theirs and ours.
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God at all times for you, because of the grace of God given to you in Christ Jesus,
because in him you have been enriched in everything, in all speech and all knowledge,
just as the testimony of God was confirmed among you,
so that you may lack nothing and fall short in no gift, as you await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
who will also strengthen you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful, through whom you were called into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

I appeal to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same thing and that there be no divisions among you, for you were united in the same mind and the same understanding.
For I have been informed about you, my brothers, by Chloe’s people, that there are quarrels among you.
What I mean is that each of you says, “I belong to Paul,” and another, “I belong to Apollos,” and another, “I belong to Cephas,” and another, “I belong to Christ.”
Is Christ divided, then? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in Paul’s name?
I thank my God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius, so that no one may say
that you were baptized in my name.
I also baptized the household of Stephanas; I do not know at all whether I baptized anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the good news—not with eloquent speech, so that the cross of Christ might not be emptied of its power.
For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will scorn the counsel of counselors.”
Where is the wise person? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this world? Has not God made the wisdom of this world foolish?
For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased to save those who believe through the foolishness of preaching.
For Jews demand a sign, and Gentiles seek wisdom,
but we shall proclaim Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
but to those who are called, both Jews and Gentiles, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For the foolishness of God is wiser than human beings, and the weakness of God is stronger than human beings.
Yet consider your own calling, brothers: not many are wise according to the flesh, not many are powerful, and not many are of noble birth.
But God chose the foolish of this world to put the wise to shame, and God chose the weak of this world to put the mighty to shame,
and God chose the lowborn of the world and the despised, and the things that are nothing, to bring to nothing the things that are,
so that no human being may boast before God.
For it is through him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
So that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
And when I came to you, brothers, I did not proclaim the testimony of God to you with any superiority of speech or wisdom.
For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
And I was with you in weakness, fear, and much trembling.
And my speech and preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with demonstrations of the Spirit and with power,
so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God.
We speak wisdom among the mature, but not the wisdom of this world or of the rulers of this world, who are passing away.
Instead, we speak God's wisdom in a hidden mystery, which God ordained before the ages for our glory.
None of the rulers of this world knew it, for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written, “What no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, God has prepared for those who love him.”
But God revealed it to us through his Spirit, for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
For who among human beings knows a person's thoughts except that person's spirit within them? Likewise, no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.
But we received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we might know what God has freely given us.
And we speak of these things not in words taught by human eloquence, but in the teaching of the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.
For the natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, because they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, since they are examined spiritually.
But the spiritual person examines everything, and is himself examined by no one.
For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to become his counselor? But we have the mind of Christ.
And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to people of the flesh.
As infants in Christ, I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, because you were not yet able to take it. Even now you are still unable, because you are still people of the flesh.
For when there are strife and jealousy among you, are you not people of the flesh, behaving in a merely human way?
When one of you says, “I belong to Paul,” and another, “I belong to Apollos,” are you not merely human? What, then, is Paul, or what is Apollos?
Servants through whom you believed, each as the Lord granted him.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.
So neither the one who planted nor the one who watered is anything, but God, who made it grow.
The one who planted and the one who watered are one, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's cultivated field, God's building.
According to the grace of God given to me, I laid a foundation like a wise master builder, but someone else builds on it. Let each person be careful how he builds.
For no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, grass, or reeds,
each person's work will be revealed, for the Day will test it, because it will be revealed by fire, and the fire will test what sort of work each person has done.
If anyone's work that he has built remains, he will receive a reward.
And if anyone's work is burned up, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, though as if through fire.
Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in you?
If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy him, for God's temple is holy, and you are that temple.
Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you wishes to be wise in this world, let him become a fool so that he may become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness before God, because it is written, “He catches the wise in their own cunning.”
And again: “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile.”
Therefore, let no one boast about human beings.
For everything is yours, whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, whether the world or life or death, whether things present or things to come—everything is yours.
You belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
Let people regard us in this way: as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries.
Now it is required among commanders that a person be found faithful.
But to me it is of little account if I am judged by you or by anyone at all. I do not even examine myself.
For I am aware of nothing against myself, but that does not make me righteous, for it is the Lord who examines me.

Therefore, do not judge before the appointed time, until the Lord comes. He will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the intentions of hearts. Then each person will receive praise from God.

Brothers, I have applied these things figuratively to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that through us you may learn not to think beyond what is written, and so that you may not become puffed up in favor of one person against another.
Now, who sets you apart? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?
Already you are full! Already you have become rich! You have become kings without us! If only you really were kings, so that we too might reign with you!
It seems to me that God has placed us apostles last, like people condemned to death, for we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels, and to human beings.
We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are powerful. You are honored, but we are dishonored.
Up to this very hour we have been hungry and thirsty, naked, beaten, and without a settled home.
And we have labored with our own hands. When people reviled us, we blessed them; when they persecuted us, we endured it.
When they insulted us, we pleaded with them. We have become a byword of ridicule to the whole world, everyone's refuse, even to this day.
I do not write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.
Even if you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you do not have many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
Therefore, I urge you to imitate me.
For this reason I sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every church.
Some have become arrogant, as though I were not coming to you.
But I will come to you very soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the words of those who have become arrogant, but their power.
For the kingdom of God is not a matter of words, but of power.
Now, what do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness, righteousness, and humility?
Why, indeed, is sexual immorality reported among you at all—and such sexual immorality as is not even found among the Gentiles, namely, that someone has his father's wife?
And you have become arrogant, rather than mourning so that the one who did this deed might be removed from among you.
For although I am absent in body, I am near in spirit, and I have already passed judgment on the one who acted in this way, as though I were present.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together, and my spirit is with you, along with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
hand such a person over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough?
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch of dough, as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover sacrifice, has been slaughtered.
Therefore, let us celebrate the feast, not with old yeast, nor with the yeast of evil and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in that letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
I did not mean the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy, or robbers, or idolaters; otherwise you would have to leave the world itself.

But now I have written to you not to associate with anyone called a brother who is sexually immoral, or an idolater, or greedy, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or a robber. Do not even eat bread with such a person.
For what have I to do with judging outsiders? Is it not those inside whom you are to judge?
And God will judge outsiders. Remove the evil person from among you.
Does anyone among you, when he has a dispute with his neighbor, dare to go to court before the unrighteous rather than before the saints?
Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge trivial cases?
Do you not know that we will judge angels, let alone earthly matters?
If you undertake court cases concerning earthly matters, you appoint as judges those held in contempt in the church.
I say this to your shame. Is there really no one wise among you who can decide a dispute between his brothers?
Instead, brother goes to court against brother, and that before unbelievers.
Indeed, it is already a complete failure among you that there are lawsuits among you at all. Why not rather be defrauded? Why not rather be oppressed?
Instead, you defraud and oppress others, and you do this even to your brothers.
Do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers,
nor effeminate men, nor men who have sex with males, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor robbers will inherit the kingdom of God.
And some of you were such people. But you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
Everything is permissible for me, but not everything is beneficial. Everything is permissible for me, but I will not come under anyone’s power.
Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food, but God will bring both it and them to an end. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
And God, who raised the Lord, will also raise you by his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall we then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? Certainly not!
Do you not know that whoever joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For he says, “The two shall become one body.”
And whoever joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with him.
Flee from sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside his own body, but whoever commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and that you are not your own masters?
For you were bought at a price. Glorify God in your bodies.
Now concerning what you wrote to me: it is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman.
But because of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
Let the husband give his wife what he owes her, and likewise the wife to her husband.
For the wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does. Likewise, the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

Do not deprive one another, except by mutual agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to your vows. Then come together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your abstinence.
I say this as a concession, not as a command.
For I wish that everyone were as I am. But each has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that way.
But to the unmarried and the widows I say: it is good for them to remain as I am.
But if they cannot exercise self-control, let them marry, for it is better to marry than to burn.
But to the married I give this command—not I, but the Lord: a wife must not separate from her husband.
But if she separates, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And the husband must not leave his wife.
But to the others I give this instruction, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is willing to live with him, let him not leave her.
And if a woman has an unbelieving husband, and he is willing to live with her, let her not leave her husband.
For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through her husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
But if the unbeliever separates, let that person separate. The brother or sister is under no obligation in such circumstances, for God has called us to peace.
For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
However, let each person live according to what the Lord has allotted to them and as God has called them. This is what I command in all the churches.
Was anyone called while circumcised? Let him not seek to become uncircumcised. Was anyone called while uncircumcised? Let him not be circumcised.
For circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing; what matters is keeping God's commandments.
But let each person remain in the condition in which they were called.
Were you called as a slave? Do not let it trouble you. But if you can become free, that would be better for you.
For the slave who was called in the Lord is the Lord's freedman. Likewise, the free person who was called is Christ's slave.
You were bought at a price. Do not become slaves of human beings.
Brothers, let each person remain before God in the condition in which they were called.
Now concerning virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give advice as someone who has received mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.
I think it is good to remain as one is: because of the distress that is upon us, it is good for a person to remain that way.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
For if you marry, you have not sinned, and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But such people will have bodily troubles, and I would spare you.
But I say this, brothers: the time has grown short. From now on, let those who have wives be as though they had none,
and those who weep as though they did not weep, and those who rejoice as though they did not rejoice, and those who buy as though they possessed nothing,
and those who use the world as though they did not enjoy it, for the splendor of this world is passing away.
But I want you to be free from care. For the unmarried man is concerned with the Lord's affairs, how he may please the Lord,
and the married man is concerned with the world's affairs, how he may please his wife.

And there is a distinction between the married woman and the virgin. For the virgin is concerned with the Lord's affairs, so that she may be holy in body and spirit, while the married woman is concerned with the world's affairs, how she may please her husband.
I say this for your benefit, not to put a noose around you, but for propriety and devotion to the Lord without distraction.
But if anyone thinks he is acting shamefully toward his virgin, if she is past the proper age and it must be so, let him do what he wishes. He does not sin; let her marry.
But the man who stands firm in his heart, who is under no necessity and has authority over his own will, and who has decided in his heart to keep his virgin unmarried, does well.
So the man who gives his virgin in marriage does well, and the man who does not give her in marriage does even better.
A wife is bound as long as her husband is alive. But if her husband falls asleep in death, she is free to marry whomever she wishes, but only in the Lord.
But she is happier if she remains as she is, according to my advice. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
Now concerning sacrifices to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge makes people proud, but love builds them up.
If anyone wishes to know something, that person does not yet know as they ought to know.
But whoever loves God is known by him.
Now concerning eating food offered in sacrifice, we know that idols are nothing in the world and that there is no God except one.
For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many gods and many lords—
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom all things come and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things exist and through whom we exist.
But not everyone has this knowledge. Some, whose conscience is still affected by idols, eat the food as something sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, because it is weak, is defiled.
But food does not bring us before God. We lose nothing if we do not eat, and we gain nothing if we do eat.
But be careful that this freedom of yours does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
If someone sees you, who have this knowledge, reclining at a meal in an idol's temple, will not that person's conscience, clothed in weakness, then be encouraged to eat food offered in sacrifice?
And through your knowledge the weak brother for whom Christ died will perish.
In this way, by wronging the brothers and wounding their weak conscience, one sins against Christ.
Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I do not cause my brother to stumble.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen our Lord Jesus Christ with my own eyes? Are you not my work in the Lord?
Even if I am not an apostle to others, I am to you, for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
This is my answer to those who question me.
Do we not have the right to eat and drink?
Do we not have the right to take wives who are sisters in the faith along with us, as do the other apostles, the Lord's brothers, and Cephas?
Or is it only Barnabas and I who do not have the right to refrain from working?
Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not partake of the flock's milk?
Am I saying this merely in human terms? Does not the law say the same thing?
For it is written in the law of Moses: "You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing." Is God concerned about oxen?
Does he not say this for our sake? For it was written for our sake, because the one who sows ought to sow in hope, and the one who [?] ought to hope to share in the yield.
If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it a great matter if we reap material things from you?
If others enjoy this right over you, do we not have it even more? Yet we have not exercised this right, but endure everything so that we may not become any hindrance to the gospel.
Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat from the temple, and those who serve at the altar share in what comes from the altar?
In the same way, the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the gospel should live from the gospel.
But I have made use of none of these rights, nor have I written this so that such provision should be made for me. It would be better for me to die than for anyone to make my boast empty.
For if I proclaim the gospel, I have nothing to boast about, because necessity is laid upon me. But woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
If I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship.
What, then, is my reward? That when I proclaim the gospel, I offer it free of charge, so that I do not abuse my authority in the gospel.
For although I was free from everyone, I made myself a slave to everyone, so that I might win many.
Among the Jews I became like a Jew, so that I might win the Jews.

Among those under the law I became like those under the law—not that I myself was under the law, but so that I might also win those under the law. Among those without the law I became like one without the law—not that I was without God's law, but under Christ's law—so that I might win those without the law.
Among the weak I became like one who was weak, so that I might win the weak. I became all things among all people, so that I might perhaps save some.
I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in it.
Do you not know that those who run in the race all run, but only one receives the prize of victory? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
Everyone who competes exercises self-control in everything. They do it to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one.
So I run, not as though without a clear goal; I fight, not as though merely beating the air.
But I discipline my body and bring it into submission, lest, after preaching to others, I myself should be found unfit.
I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea.
And they were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
And they all ate the same spiritual food.
And they all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock itself was Christ.
But God was not pleased with many of them, for they fell dead there in the wilderness.
And this happened as an example for us, so that we should not desire evil things as they desired them.
And do not become idolaters as some of them did, as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”
And let us not commit sexual immorality as some of them did, and twenty-four thousand fell in a single day.
And let us not put the Lord to the test as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
And let us not grumble as some of them did, and perished at the hands of the destroyer.
But all these things happened to them as examples, and were written for our instruction, upon whom the end of the ages has come.
Therefore, let anyone who thinks he stands firm be careful lest he fall.

No temptation has come upon you except what is common to humanity. But God is faithful: he will not let you be tempted beyond your strength, but with the temptation he will also provide a way out, so that you can endure it.
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
I speak to you as wise people; judge for yourselves what I say.
The cup of blessing that we bless—is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break—is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?
For we, though many, are one bread, one body, because we all partake of that one bread.
Consider Israel by physical descent: are not those who eat the sacrifices sharers in the altar?
What, then, am I saying? That something sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that idols themselves are anything?
Rather, what the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. I do not want you to share with demons, for you cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons.
And you cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
Are we to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he is?
Everything is permissible for me, but not everything is beneficial. Everything is permissible for me, but not everything builds up.
Let no one seek only his own good, but also his neighbor's.
Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, without questioning it for the sake of conscience.
For the earth belongs to the Lord, with all that fills it.
If one of the unbelievers invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, without questioning it for the sake of conscience.
But if someone says to you, “This has been sacrificed,” do not eat it, for the sake of the person who informed you and for the sake of conscience.
But I mean the conscience—not one's own, but one's neighbor's. For why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience at all?
If I partake with gratitude, why am I denounced for something for which I give thanks?
Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do everything for the glory of God.
Do not cause Jews, Gentiles, or the church of God to stumble.
Just as I please everyone in everything, not seeking my own benefit but that of the many, so that they may be saved.
Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ.
I praise you because you remember me in everything and hold to the traditions just as I handed them down to you.
I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is her husband, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is the same as if she were shaved.
For if a woman does not cover herself, let her cut her hair short. But if it is improper for a woman to cut her hair short or shave it, let her cover herself.
A man ought not to cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God; but a woman is the glory of her husband.
For man is not from woman, but woman from man.
For man was not created for woman, but woman for man.
For this reason a woman ought to put a covering on her head because of the angels.
Nevertheless, in the Lord neither is woman without man, nor man without woman.
For just as woman is from man, so man is also from woman, but everything is from God.
But judge for yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray before God with her head uncovered?
Does not nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him?
But if a woman has long hair, it is her glory, because her hair has been given to her as a covering.
But if anyone wishes to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.
But in giving this instruction, I am not praising you, because you are moving not toward what is better but toward what is worse.
First, when you gather together in church, I hear that there are divisions among you, and I believe it to some extent.
Indeed, there must also be divisions among you, so that those among you who are approved may become evident.
So when you gather together, the Lord's house is not a place for you to eat bread.
For each person goes ahead and eats his own supper, and one is hungry while another is drunk.
Do you not have houses in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and shame the poor? What shall I say? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.
For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when he was being betrayed, took bread,
gave thanks, broke it, and said, “This is my body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
Likewise, after supper he also took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, whenever you drink it, in remembrance of me.”
For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.
Therefore, whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord's cup unworthily will be guilty concerning the Lord's body and blood.
Let a person examine himself, and then eat of the bread and drink from the cup.
For whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment upon himself, because he does not discern the Lord's body.
For this very reason, many among you are weak and sick, and many have even fallen asleep.
For if we examined ourselves, we would not be condemned.
And when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned with the world.
Therefore, brothers, when you gather together to eat, wait for one another.
But if anyone is hungry, let him eat in his own house, so that you do not gather together for condemnation. As for the other matters, I will give instructions when I come.
Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant.
You know how, when you were Gentiles, you used to go back and forth to mute idols.
Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus is accursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
Although there are different kinds of gifts, the Spirit is the same.
Although there are different kinds of service, the Lord is the same.
Although there are different kinds of workings, God is the same, who works everything in everyone.
But to each person a manifestation of the Spirit is given for that person's benefit.
To one, a word of wisdom is given by the Spirit; to another, a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit;
to another, faith through the same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing through the same Spirit;
to another, the working of miracles; to another, prophecy; to another, discernment of spirits; to another, different kinds of tongues; to another, interpretation of tongues.
But one and the same Spirit works all these things and distributes them to each person as he wishes.
Just as the body is one and has many members, and all the many members of the body are one body, so also is Christ.
For through one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, whether slaves or free, and we all drank of one Spirit.
For the body is not one member but many.
If the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it cease to belong to the body.
And if the ear says, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it cease to belong to the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would the ear be? And if everything were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
But now God has placed the members, each one of them, in the body as he wished.
But if everything were one member, where would the body be?
But now there are many members and one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, “I have no need of you,” nor again can the head say to the feet, “I have no need of you.”
Rather, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are necessary.
And those parts of the body that seem less honorable, we treat with greater honor, and our shameful parts receive even greater modesty.
Our presentable parts have no such need, for God has joined the body together and given even greater honor to the part that lacked it,
so that there may be no divisions in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.
And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; and if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
Now you are Christ's body and members among his members.

And these are those whom God has appointed in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, helpers, leaders, various kinds of tongues, and interpretations of tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
But eagerly seek the better gifts. And I will show you an even more excellent way.
If I speak in the tongues of humans and angels but do not have love, I have become like sounding bronze or clanging cymbals.
And if I have prophecy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, enough to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
And if I distribute all my possessions to the poor and hand over my body to be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
Love is patient and kind. Love does not envy, does not boast, and is not proud.
It does not behave rudely, does not seek its own interests, is not provoked, and does not think evil.
It does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices in truth.
It bears everything, believes everything, hopes in all things, and endures everything.
Love never fails. But prophecies will come to an end, tongues will fall silent, and knowledge will come to an end.
For we know only in part, and we prophesy only in part.
But when completeness comes, what is partial will come to an end.
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, thought like a child, and reasoned like a child. But when I became a man, I put away childish things.
Now we see as through a mirror, in an image, but then face to face. Now I understand only in part, but then I will know just as he also knew me.
But now these three remain: faith, hope, and love. And the greatest of these is love.
Pursue love and eagerly seek spiritual gifts, especially that you may prophesy.
For whoever speaks in tongues speaks not to people but to God, because no one understands; rather, in the spirit he speaks mysteries.
But whoever prophesies speaks to people for their building up, encouragement, and comfort.
Whoever speaks in tongues builds himself up, but whoever prophesies builds up the church.
I want all of you to speak in tongues, but even more to prophesy. For whoever prophesies is greater than whoever speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may be built up.
But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what benefit will I bring you unless I speak through revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?

Likewise, when lifeless things produce sound, whether a flute or a harp, if they make no distinction between the notes, how will anyone recognize what is being played on the flute or sounded on the harp?
For if the trumpet gives an indistinct sound, who will prepare for battle?
Likewise, if you do not express the message clearly with your tongues, how will what is spoken be understood? You will then be like people speaking into the air.
For there are so many kinds of sounds in the world, and nothing is without a sound.
Now, if I do not know the meaning of the sound, I will be a foreigner to the person speaking to me, and the person speaking to me will be a foreigner to me.
Likewise, since you are eager for spiritual gifts, seek to abound in them for the building up of the church.
Therefore, anyone who speaks in tongues should pray that they may also interpret.
If I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
What, then, should I do? I will pray with my spirit, and I will also pray with my mind. I will sing psalms with my spirit, and I will also sing psalms with my mind.
Otherwise, if you give a blessing with your spirit, how will someone who occupies the place of the uninstructed say “Amen” to your praise, since they do not understand what you are saying?
For you give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.
I thank God that I speak in a tongue more than all of you.
But in the church I would rather speak five words with my mind, so that I may instruct others too, than many words in a tongue.
Brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Rather, be children in regard to evil, but be mature in your thinking.
For it is also written in the law: “In foreign tongues and with foreign lips I will speak to this people, yet even then they will not listen to me.”
So tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers, while prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.
So if the whole church comes together in one place and everyone speaks in tongues, and uninstructed people or unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are mad?
But if everyone prophesies and an unbeliever or an uninstructed person comes in, that person is reproved by everyone and examined by everyone.
The secrets of their heart become known, and then they will fall facedown and worship God, acknowledging that God is truly among you.
What, then, should be done, brothers? When you gather in one place, each of you may have a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Let everything be done for building up.
If anyone speaks in tongues, let two speak, or at most three, one at a time, and let one person interpret.
But if there is no one to interpret, let the speaker remain silent in the church and speak inwardly to themselves and to God.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others evaluate.
But if something is revealed to another person sitting there, let the first speaker be silent.
For you can all prophesy one at a time, so that everyone may learn and everyone may be encouraged.
For the spirits of prophets are themselves subject to prophets.
For God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.
Let women remain silent in all the churches, for they are not permitted to speak, but must be subject, as the law itself also says.
But if they wish to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is improper for a woman to speak in church.
Did the word of God come from you, or did it reach you alone?
If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize that what I have written to you is the Lord’s commandments.
But if anyone is ignorant, let him remain ignorant.
Therefore, brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
And let everything among you be done decently and in order.
I make known to you, brothers, my gospel, which I preached to you, which you also received, and in which you stand firm,
through which you are also saved, if you hold fast to the word with which I preached it—unless you believed in vain.
For I handed on to you first what I myself also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
and that he was buried, and that he rose on the third day according to the Scriptures,
and that he appeared to Cephas, and then to the Twelve.
Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, many of whom remain until now, though some have fallen asleep.
And then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
Last of all, he appeared also to me, as to an unworthy person.
For I am the least of the apostles, and am not even worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain. Rather, I labored more than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God that is with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we preached, and this is what you believed.
But if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ has not risen, our preaching is in vain, and your faith is also in vain.
And we are found to be false witnesses about God, because we testified about God that he raised Christ, whom he did not in fact raise if the dead do not rise.
But if the dead do not rise, then Christ has not risen either.
And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile, and you still remain in the same sins.
So then, have those who fell asleep in Christ indeed perished?
If we have hoped in Christ only in this life, we are more pitiable than all other people.
But now Christ has risen from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
For death came through a man, and the resurrection of the dead also comes through a man.
As all die in Adam, so also all will be made alive in Christ.
Each in his own order: first Christ, and then those who belong to Christ at his coming.
Then comes the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he abolishes every authority and every rule and power.
For he must reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be abolished is death, and he has subjected everything under his feet.
But when he says, “Everything has been subjected to him,” it is clear that this excludes the one who subjected everything to him.
But when everything has been subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to the one who subjected everything to him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will those who are baptized for the dead do? If the dead really do not rise, why are they baptized for them at all?
And why do we struggle at every moment?
And we die every day—I swear, brothers, by my pride in you, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If, for human reasons, I fought wild beasts at Ephesus, what benefit was that to me? If the dead do not rise, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Do not be deceived: evil words corrupt good character.
Come to your senses as you ought, and do not sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
But someone will say, “How do the dead rise? And with what kind of body will they come?”
You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
And what you sow is not the body that is to come into being, but a bare grain, whether of wheat or of some other seed.
And God gives it a body as he wills, and to each seed its own body.
Not all flesh is the same flesh: human flesh is one kind, the flesh of animals another, the flesh of birds another, and the flesh of fish another.
There are both heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly bodies is one kind, and the glory of the earthly bodies another.
The sun has one glory, the moon another glory, and the stars another glory; and one star surpasses another in glory.
So it is also with the resurrection of the dead: it is sown in decay and rises without decay.
It is sown in dishonor and rises in glory; it is sown in weakness and rises in power.
A natural body is sown, and a spiritual body rises. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
So it is also written: “The first man, Adam, became a living being”; the second Adam became a life-giving spirit.
But the spiritual is not first; rather, the natural comes first, and then the spiritual.
The first man was from the earth, made of dust; but the second man is the Lord from heaven.
As is the one made of dust, so are those made of dust; and as is the heavenly one, so are those who are heavenly.
And just as we have put on the image of the one made of dust, let us also put on the image of the heavenly one.
But I say this, brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does corruption inherit incorruptibility.
Now I tell you a mystery: we will all fall asleep, but not all of us
will be changed, suddenly, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise without corruption, and we will be changed.
For this corruptible body must put on incorruptibility, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
But when this mortal body puts on immortality, and this corruptible body puts on incorruptibility, then the saying that was written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O Hades, is your sting?
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gave us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, remain unmoved, and always abound in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain before the Lord.
Now concerning the collection for the saints, do just as I instructed the churches of the Galatians.
On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside for himself whatever he has been able to save as he prospers.
This is so that collections will not have to be made when I come. When I arrive, I will send those whom you approve, with letters, to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
And if it is fitting for me to go as well, they will go with me.
But I will come to you when I pass through Macedonia. But when I have traveled through Macedonia,
perhaps I will stay with you, or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I am to go.
For I do not want to see you now merely in passing. I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
But for now I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,
because a great and important door has been opened to me, and there are many opponents.
Now if Timothy comes, see that he has nothing to fear among you, for he does the Lord’s work, just as I do.
Let no one despise him. Send him on his way in peace so that he may come to me, for I am expecting him together with the brothers.
As for our brother Apollos, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but he was not willing to come now. He will come when he has the opportunity.
Keep watch, stand firm in the faith, be courageous, and be strong.
Let everything you do be done with love.
I appeal to you, brothers: you know the household of Stephanas and Fortunatus, who are the first converts among the Achaeans and have devoted themselves to serving the saints.
So that you too may submit to such people and to everyone who works and labors with them.
I rejoiced at the arrival of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, because they made up for your absence.
For they refreshed my spirit and yours. So recognize such people.
The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the church in their house.
All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
This greeting is in my own hand, Paul’s.
If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus, let him be accursed. Maranatha!
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
And my love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen. The first letter to the Corinthians was written from Ephesus and sent through Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus.
